When a layer has a parent, it takes on the parent's position, scale and rotation, and still runs its own animation on top. A null is an invisible layer used as that parent. You put it where the group should turn or scale from, attach the group to it, and animate only the null. Hatch is already set up this way: it follows Hatch Rig. Here's the idea. When a layer has a parent, it picks up the parent's moves while still running its own animation. A null makes a good parent because it's an invisible handle. You can see this in your comp already: Hatch follows Hatch Rig. Children inherit their parent's position, scale and rotation, but not its opacity or effects. A null never shows in the render, so it can't add its own look to the group.
